# Attachment Access Functions

A reusable compute definition for registering attachment permission documents and installing a designated authority party. It inherits activation, participant access, party mapping and amendment functions. Functions act in the document where they execute; a callable function alone establishes neither a viewer’s permission nor an obligation.

## Attachment access registration

`registerAccessPublic(input)` delegates to `registerAccess(input)`. `input.documents` must contain one to sixteen existing, initialized `Timeline Access` publications. Each must have a `Public Timeline Channel` at `/contracts/provider`, an initialization document at `/contracts/initialized/document`, and provider history at `/contracts/checkpoint/entries/provider`. Missing `documents` defaults to an empty list and is rejected.

Registration requires `call/requireExactDocumentVersion` to be exactly `true`, and `call/channel` must be a party key in `/activation/parties`, identifying a party lead. It rejects frozen parties and requires `/activation/allowNewParties` even when the submitted documents are duplicates. These checks treat missing `frozen` and `allowNewParties` as `false`.

The execution constant `key` determines `/attachmentAccess_<key>`. Registration stores publication references under zero-based numeric keys, copies each publication’s provider channel into `/contracts/attachmentAccess_<key>_<index>`, and installs a corresponding `_refresh` workflow containing `Refresh Activation`. The registered reference paths are appended to `/activation/accessPaths`, using an empty list when that field is absent.

If the registration path already exists, the number and publication identities must match at every position. An exact match returns `outcome: duplicate` without adding changes; any mismatch rejects with `ATTACHMENT_ACCESS_ALREADY_REGISTERED`. A new registration returns `outcome: acceptedNew`. Registration itself does not recompute activation or change the provider’s permission sets.

## Authority installation

`addAuthority(input)` accepts `replacement`, which must include `lead.channel`. It requires exact-version review, an existing party-lead `call/channel`, and unfrozen parties. If the designated authority party already exists, only its own lead channel may replace it.

`installAuthority(input)` forces `input.party` to the execution constant `authority`, regardless of a supplied target. It checks freezing, permits a new party only when `allowNewParties` is enabled, and validates the replacement and resulting participant access. Unlike `addAuthority`, this helper does not itself check exact-version review or the invoking party lead; its caller must supply the appropriate authorization context. Values for the `authority` and `key` constants are not supplied here.

The authority key and all `replacement.representatives` keys must be nonempty text containing none of `.`, `/`, `~` or `__`. The replacement replaces the whole party entry. Party data can include `business`, `displayName`, `partyId`, `readerKeys`, a lead and additional representatives; descriptive identity information is not evidence of authority.

On success, installation writes roster channels and lead approval/update handlers under `/contracts`, rejecting names already occupied outside the previous roster’s generated contracts. It clears all `approved` entries, appends a newly added authority to `required`, increments `revision` using `1` when absent, writes the result of `computeState` to `/activation`, emits `Party Changed` with `party` and `revision`, and returns `true`. Even an unchanged replacement follows this update path. This helper calls `computeState` directly, so it does not perform the additional terms reconciliation or activation-transition events of `commitState`.

## Participant access and activation

Access validation covers every party’s `lead.channel` and each additional representative’s `channel`. `External Channel` instances bypass timeline permission checks. Other channels must be `Timeline Channel` instances. For each such channel, at least one document referenced by `accessPaths` must match its timeline and provider and contain at least one allowed key from every reader group. All groups must be satisfied within that matching access document.

Reader groups combine `/activation/readers` with each party’s `readerKeys` and each additional representative’s `readerKeys`, under party keys and `<party>__<representative>` keys. Roster-derived groups replace same-named supplied groups. Missing key lists become empty groups, which cannot satisfy a private timeline’s access check. Missing `accessPaths`, `readers` and roster collections use empty collections in these checks.

`computeState` sets `accessReady` and `functional` from access validation, including pending `accessRequests` additions whose `expectedRevision` matches the current revision. `termsAccepted` requires every party in `required` to have approval and every recorded `/activation/terms/fields` value to match its document path. Missing individual approvals count as unapproved during computation; missing `required` and recorded fields use empty collections. `active` additionally requires the document not to be `closed`.

Computed `status` is `CLOSED`, `WAITING_FOR_ACCESS`, `SUSPENDED_ACCESS`, `AWAITING_ACCEPTANCE` or `ACTIVE`; suspension distinguishes previously activated documents using `everActivated`. `reason` reports missing access first, then missing acceptance, otherwise an empty string. An empty reason alone does not establish that the document is active. These are execution rules, not permission to interpret absent stored state as completed or false.

`refresh` initializes terms when needed, commits recalculated activation and refreshes pending access-request readiness. `commitState` reconciles initial channels, tracks `everActivated`, and emits `Document Activated`, `Document Access Suspended` or `Document Access Restored` for its defined transitions. Roster or required-party changes also revise existing terms references and supersede pending negotiation authority; configured negotiation paths cause approvals to be cleared.

## Inherited operations

`approve` requires exact-version review, a party lead, the current `input.revision` and valid participant access. With nonempty `/clauses/activation/parameters/negotiation/allowedPaths`, a text `termsRef` is required; any supplied reference must match `/activation/terms/ref`. `approveWithTerms` exposes both fields. An already approved party returns `true`; a new approval commits state and emits `Terms Accepted`. Approval can contribute to activation but does not independently guarantee it.

`updatePartyPublic` delegates to `updateParty`. Its optional `party` defaults to the invoking party; another existing party cannot be replaced. New parties require `allowNewParties`. It applies the same replacement, name, access and contract-conflict checks described above, clears approvals and increments the revision, but uses `commitState`.

Admission support records revision-specific additions, registers their access evidence and emits `Party Access Update Requested` where existing parties need additional access. Stale or already recorded requests are ignored. Such events request action; they do not grant permission or prove completion. `admitApprovedParties` requires unfrozen parties, matching `expectedRevision`, a nonempty configured `admission.approvers` policy, consistent existing identities and valid resulting access. It installs additions, advances the revision and emits `Party Changed`; this helper does not itself collect approver votes or append additions to `required`.

Inherited party mapping resolves declared roles to party identities without granting access or consent. Main identity comparisons require matching lead channels and equal, nonempty, duplicate-free primary reader-key sets. Inherited amendment helpers use supplied `bindings`, `parameters` and state: proposals require a current revision, an allowed path, editable terms and a valid unused `proposalId`; `preservePending` prevents replacing another pending proposal. Approvals require a configured approver and the current proposal. The field replacement occurs only after all configured approvals; `acceptedNew` can therefore mean a newly recorded approval rather than an applied amendment.

Attachment registration checks publication type and the presence of provider, initialization and history fields; it does not invoke the inherited stronger executable-policy validator or test participant coverage. Provider-owned permission changes and confirmed activation must be distinguished from successful registration.
